findings: Owner request 2026-11-09: practice mcqs for Chapter 3 in the same format as the Physics chapter practice, long questions in the Computer Science Board shape (8 marks each) (English and Roman Urdu), written from the chapter; not printed in the book. 67 questions numbered 1-67; by section: 3.1 12, 3.2 55. Keys: {'a': 16, 'b': 17, 'c': 17, 'd': 17}.

Covers every part of the chapter in book order: OOP and its benefits (modularity, reusability, maintenance), classes and objects, self and __init__, encapsulation and why it matters, public, protected and private members with name mangling, inheritance (single, multiple, multilevel, base and derived class, overriding, super()), polymorphism, its two types, compile-time style overloading with default and variable-length arguments, and runtime polymorphism by overriding. None repeats the chapter exercise. Every program was run in Python 3 and its real output (or real error) is the key. Book correction followed: a private member has two underscores (__private_variable), not one as in the printed Figure 3.2.
Every question carries a book_ref (topic id and exact words of that topic's English lesson), verified by tools.py.
The Roman Urdu file has the same checkpoints, order and book_refs; each prompt keeps the English question with the Roman Urdu meaning in brackets.
Drafts for the academic review (second-person review before publication).
